name: Weak strategy: Spotify hardware, enthusiasm without economics or competitive analysis
scratchpadNotes: headphones yes! brand. playlists button. speakers too

messages.text: Spotify is thinking about launching its own premium headphones and smart speakers. Should it?
Yes, I think they definitely should. Spotify has a huge brand and lots of people love it, so if they made headphones people would buy them. It's like how Apple has AirPods.
What would make Spotify headphones better than what Apple, Sony or Bose sell?
They could have a Spotify button that plays your Discover Weekly right away. And they'd have better recommendations built in. Maybe also a special colour so people recognise them.
How do you think about the economics? Spotify's gross margins are pretty thin.
I think hardware would actually help with that because they get the money from selling the headphones, plus people keep paying for Premium. So it's extra revenue on top.
What about companies like Sonos and Bose that already have Spotify built in?
They would still keep Spotify in their products because everyone uses Spotify, so I don't think that's a problem.
Did you know Spotify already tried a hardware product, Car Thing, and discontinued it?
Oh, I didn't know that. Maybe it just wasn't marketed enough. Headphones are more popular than car stuff so it would be different.
Launch headphones and speakers, and do a big marketing campaign with artists. Maybe give them free to Premium Family users to start.
